chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Umar, when it is the night of Friday, angels descend from the heaven in the number of the gnats, holding in their hands pens of gold and sheets of silver. They do not write until the night of Saturday except for the Salat (prayer/blessing) upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, so increase in it.'

And he said: 'O Umar, indeed it is from the Sunnah that you send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and his household a thousand times every Friday, and a hundred times on the other days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of Salawat on Friday night according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the cosmic significance of Friday in Shia tradition, where angels record blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, linking the day to divine mercy and spiritual elevation. The specific recommendation of sending a thousand blessings on Friday and a hundred on other days underscores the Sunnah of frequent salawat, reinforcing the Imam’s role in guiding ritual practice. This emphasis on Friday night (Laylat al-Jumu'ah) as a time of angelic activity reflects broader Shia eschatological and devotional themes.
